1523.recognize_zh: H&E 組織切片可見中型淋巴樣細胞瀰漫浸潤，核圓形至不規則、染色質細緻、部分有小而明顯的核仁，胞質中等量；這些形態本身不具特異性，要確定為 T-PLL 必須結合周邊血、流式細胞儀與 TCL1 染色。
features: Diffuse infiltrate of medium-sized lymphoid cells replacing the tissue
Round to irregular or indented nuclei with fine to vesicular chromatin
Small but distinct nucleoli in a subset of cells
Moderate amounts of pale to eosinophilic cytoplasm
Scattered small dark lymphocytes, vessels and red cells; no follicles or granulomas
1523.describe_en: H&E-stained tissue section shows a diffuse infiltrate of medium-sized lymphoid cells with round to irregular nuclei, fine to vesicular chromatin, small distinct nucleoli in some cells and moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm. Scattered small mature lymphocytes and vessels are present, without follicles or granulomas. The morphology is that of an atypical medium-sized lymphoid infiltrate and is not specific on its own. In the context of known T-prolymphocytic leukemia, these findings are compatible with tissue involvement, to be confirmed by immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD7 and TCL1.

ddx.vs: DLBCL cells are larger (at least twice a small lymphocyte) with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli and are CD20/PAX5-positive.
PTCL usually shows more pleomorphic cells with a mixed inflammatory background and lacks TCL1 expression and inv(14).
Blastoid mantle cell lymphoma is a B-cell neoplasm with cyclin D1 and SOX11 positivity.
Lymphoblasts have finer blastic chromatin, scant cytoplasm and brisk mitoses and are TdT-positive.

1395.recognize_zh: 多顆大型細胞細胞質豐富，含細小紅紫色嗜苯胺藍顆粒，細胞核折疊、腎形或雙葉狀（像兩片重疊），部分細胞顆粒較少而細胞質淡灰，呈現異常早幼粒細胞的樣貌，符合（續發性）急性前骨髓細胞白血病。
features: Large cells with abundant cytoplasm and variable fine red-purple azurophilic granules
Nuclei folded, reniform or bilobed with overlapping lobes (sliding-plate appearance)
Finely dispersed chromatin; nucleoli indistinct at this resolution
Some cells with paler, less granular gray cytoplasm (hypogranular forms)
Discrete Auer rod bundles are not clearly identified in this field
Scattered small dark cells and red cells in the background
1395.describe_en: Smear, likely bone marrow aspirate, shows numerous large abnormal cells with abundant cytoplasm containing fine red-purple azurophilic granules of variable density, and folded, reniform to bilobed nuclei with fine chromatin. Some cells are relatively hypogranular with pale gray cytoplasm. Faggot cells or definite Auer rods are not clearly seen in this field. These abnormal promyelocytes are consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia; in the setting of prior cytotoxic therapy this represents therapy-related (secondary) APL, which must be confirmed urgently by PML-RARA testing given the risk of coagulopathy.

ddx.vs: Monoblasts and promonocytes have folded nuclei but gray-blue cytoplasm with sparse fine granules, strong nonspecific esterase positivity, and lack intense MPO and PML-RARA.

ddx.dx: Normal promyelocytes in marrow regeneration (e.g., post-G-CSF)
ddx.vs: Regenerating promyelocytes have round eccentric nuclei with a Golgi hof and are followed by orderly maturation, not bilobed nuclei in a monotonous population.
Shows blasts with Auer rods plus maturing neutrophils, without the predominance of abnormal bilobed granular promyelocytes.
Can mimic microgranular APL with nuclear invaginations, but is CD34/HLA-DR variably positive and PML-RARA negative.

60787.recognize_zh: 中央嗜中性球的核未分節、呈寬大腎形／花生形並有粗塊狀染色質，細胞質淡且顆粒偏少，屬低分葉的假性 Pelger-Huët 細胞（pseudo-Pelger-Huët）。
features: Mature-sized granulocyte, about 1.5-2 times red cell diameter
Hypolobated, non-segmented nucleus with a broad kidney/peanut shape
Coarsely clumped, mature chromatin inconsistent with an immature myelocyte
Pale grey-pink cytoplasm with sparse fine granules (relative hypogranularity)
Background red cells include many oval forms; scattered platelets
60787.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with a proportion of oval forms and scattered platelets. The central neutrophil has a hypolobated, non-segmented, broad kidney- to peanut-shaped nucleus with coarsely clumped mature chromatin, and pale cytoplasm with relatively sparse fine granules. The discordance between the mature chromatin and the lack of segmentation indicates a pseudo-Pelger-Huët change. Findings are consistent with pseudo-Pelger-Huët neutrophils; in the stated post-transplant setting on mycophenolate this is likely drug-related, and myelodysplasia should not be diagnosed on this basis alone.

ddx.vs: Morphology is identical; MDS requires persistent multilineage dysplasia, cytopenias and supportive cytogenetic/molecular findings in the absence of drug or other causes.
The inherited anomaly affects nearly all neutrophils uniformly with normal granulation and is lifelong, whereas acquired forms are partial and often hypogranular.
Metamyelocytes have less condensed chromatin and more abundant specific granules, and bands have a thin C- or S-shaped curved nucleus rather than a broad dense peanut shape.

115.recognize_zh: 低倍下淋巴結被密集、背靠背、缺乏套區的濾泡取代；高倍可見濾泡內混有大量中心母細胞（centroblast，大、空泡狀染色質、周邊多個核仁），而免疫染色 BCL2 在濾泡內強陽性，LMO2/HGAL 等生發中心標記陽性，支持 CD10 陰性的濾泡性淋巴瘤。
features: Effacement of nodal architecture by numerous crowded, back-to-back neoplastic follicles with attenuated or absent mantle zones

Follicles composed of a mixture of small cleaved centrocytes and many large centroblasts with vesicular chromatin and multiple peripheral nucleoli (black arrows), with admixed follicular dendritic cells and histiocytes that must be excluded from the count
No solid sheets of centroblasts in the sampled fields (no grade 3B/DLBCL component)
Interfollicular areas with high endothelial venules and small lymphocytes

IHC: diffuse membranous B-cell marker (likely CD20); strong cytoplasmic BCL2 in follicles; nuclear LMO2 (with endothelial internal control) and cytoplasmic HGAL within follicles; nuclear-marker labeling (likely BCL6/Ki-67) concentrated in follicles
Touch imprint shows a mixed population of intermediate to large lymphoid cells with open chromatin and visible nucleoli
115.describe_en: CT of the neck shows an enlarged lower cervical/supraclavicular lymph node (arrow). Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the architecture by closely packed, back-to-back follicles lacking well-formed mantle zones, with intervening vascular interfollicular stroma. At high power the follicles contain a mixture of centrocytes and numerous centroblasts, which exceed 15 per high-power field, while solid sheets of large cells are not seen in these fields; follicular dendritic cells and histiocytes are distinguished from centroblasts by their pale, bilobed or reniform nuclei and delicate small nucleoli. Immunohistochemistry shows a diffuse B-cell population with strong BCL2 expression within the follicles, and the germinal center markers LMO2 and HGAL are positive, while only scattered non-neoplastic cells are highlighted on one stain (label not provided; the report states CD10 is negative). Findings are consistent with relapsed follicular lymphoma, grade 3A, CD10-negative, without a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma component in the images shown.

ddx.vs: Reactive follicles are separated, polarized with tingible-body macrophages and intact mantle zones, and are BCL2-negative within germinal centers, unlike the crowded BCL2-positive follicles here.
Grade 3B shows solid sheets of centroblasts without residual centrocytes and DLBCL shows diffuse areas, whereas these follicles retain admixed centrocytes and no diffuse sheets are seen.

ddx.dx: Nodal marginal zone lymphoma with follicular colonization
ddx.vs: Marginal zone lymphoma consists of monocytoid/centrocyte-like cells lacking germinal center markers (LMO2, HGAL, BCL6 negative), whereas this CD10-negative lesion expresses LMO2 and HGAL.
Grade 1-2 has 15 or fewer centroblasts per HPF, whereas the high-power field here contains numerous centroblasts above that threshold.

115.stain: H&E; Romanowsky imprint; IHC (CD20, BCL2, LMO2, HGAL)
captions: Axial CT neck: enlarged lower cervical/supraclavicular lymph node (arrow)
Touch imprint: mixed intermediate and large lymphoid cells with open chromatin and nucleoli
H&E low power: nodal effacement by crowded back-to-back follicles
H&E low-medium power: closely packed follicles lacking mantle zones
H&E medium power: neoplastic follicles with vascular interfollicular stroma
H&E high power: centroblasts (black arrows) versus follicular dendritic cells/histiocytes (blue and white arrows)
IHC, membranous B-cell marker (likely CD20): diffuse positivity
IHC: only scattered small cells positive; follicular tumor cells negative
IHC LMO2 low power: nuclear staining in follicle with positive endothelial cells
IHC LMO2 high power: variable nuclear staining of follicle cells
IHC HGAL: cytoplasmic staining confined to the neoplastic follicle
IHC BCL2: strong diffuse cytoplasmic staining of follicle cells
IHC nuclear germinal-center/proliferation marker (likely BCL6 or Ki-67), low power
Same nuclear marker, high power: many positive nuclei of varying intensity

51.recognize_zh: 舌根黏膜潰瘍邊緣下方有多形性浸潤，混有大型非典型、類 Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg（HRS-like）細胞，EBER 原位雜交呈大量大小不一的核陽性。再加上病人使用 methotrexate 的醫源性免疫抑制病史，應想到 EBV 陽性黏膜皮膚潰瘍（EBVMCU）。
features: Mucosal ulcer with a dense polymorphous infiltrate beneath a fibrinous/granulation-tissue edge
Scattered large atypical cells with vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei, including HRS-like forms, amid small lymphocytes and histiocytes
Vacuolated, edematous inflammatory background with apoptotic debris
Large cells show membranous IHC staining with a Golgi/dot accentuation pattern (unlabeled marker, CD30-like), plus sheets of cells with strong membranous staining (unlabeled marker, B-cell-like)
Sharp boundary between a positive-cell-rich zone and a paucicellular negative zone on IHC
EBER ISH: numerous positive nuclei across a spectrum of cell sizes
51.describe_en: Sections of base-of-tongue mucosa show an ulcer with an underlying dense, polymorphous lymphohistiocytic infiltrate. At high power there are numerous large atypical lymphoid cells, including binucleate and multilobated Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg-like cells, admixed with small lymphocytes, histiocytes and apoptotic debris in an edematous background. Immunostains highlight sheets of large cells with strong membranous positivity and a subset with membranous and Golgi-pattern staining (markers not labeled in the images; CD20/CD30 pattern), and EBER in situ hybridization is positive in many cells of varying size. In the setting of methotrexate-associated immunosuppression and a sharply circumscribed mucosal ulcer, the findings are consistent with EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer.

ddx.dx: EBV-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS
ddx.vs: EBV+ DLBCL forms a mass-forming, non-circumscribed infiltrate often with systemic or nodal disease, whereas EBVMCU is an isolated, sharply demarcated ulcer with a basal band of small T cells and regresses with reduced immunosuppression.
In cHL the HRS cells are CD15+ with weak/absent B-cell program, while the large cells here show strong B-cell marker expression, and cHL rarely presents as an isolated mucosal ulcer.
Overlapping biology; the ulcer-limited, circumscribed architecture without mass lesion or dissemination favors the EBVMCU designation, requiring clinical staging to separate.
Reactive ulcers contain only scattered EBER+ cells without sheets of atypical HRS-like large B cells as seen here.

captions: IHC (marker unlabeled): membranous and Golgi-pattern staining of large atypical cells, CD30-like
Low-power H&E: ulcerated mucosa with dense polymorphous infiltrate
High-power H&E: large atypical and HRS-like cells in a polymorphous, vacuolated background
IHC (marker unlabeled): diffuse strong membranous staining of large cells, B-cell-marker-like
IHC (marker unlabeled): sharply demarcated zone of membranous-positive large cells
EBER ISH: numerous positive nuclei of varying size

62387.recognize_zh: 兩格末梢血中的淋巴樣細胞核周邊冒出多個小而圓、深紫色的核芽，部分已與主核分開成微核（micronuclei），像一串小泡附在核緣；左格旁邊有一顆正常分葉中性球可比較大小，背景紅血球有棘狀（crenated）乾燥假影。這是 MBL 病人 2015 年的抹片，呈現淋巴細胞核出芽的樣貌。
features: Intermediate-sized lymphoid cells with moderately condensed chromatin and scant pale blue cytoplasm
Multiple small round dense nuclear buds at the nuclear periphery, some appearing detached as micronuclei
Adjacent segmented neutrophil (left panel) for size comparison, with normal granulation
Background red cells with crenation/echinocyte artifact; scattered platelets
62387.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows lymphoid cells of intermediate size with condensed chromatin, scant pale cytoplasm and multiple small, round, dense nuclear buds protruding from the nuclear margin, some of which appear separated as micronuclei. A normal segmented neutrophil is present for comparison. Background red cells show crenation consistent with a drying artifact, and platelets are present. In the setting of monoclonal B-cell lymphocytosis, these findings represent nuclear budding with micronucleus formation; the change is descriptive and nonspecific, and should be interpreted with flow cytometric data and comparison with subsequent smears.

ddx.dx: Crenated red cell or platelet overlying a lymphocyte
ddx.vs: Overlapping cells or platelets lie in a different focal plane and have a granular or pink staining quality, whereas true nuclear buds share the nuclear chromatin color and texture.
Karyorrhexis fragments the whole nucleus into multiple dense balls without a residual intact main nucleus, unlike these peripheral buds on a preserved nucleus.
ATLL flower cells have deeply lobulated petal-like nuclei and a CD4+/CD25+ T-cell phenotype rather than small peripheral buds on B cells.

ddx.dx: Hairy cell leukemia or villous lymphocytes
ddx.vs: These show cytoplasmic projections rather than nuclear buds, with a distinct immunophenotype (CD103, CD11c, CD25 in HCL).

60147.recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中成群的中到大型胚細胞，核大且常有凹陷或摺痕、染色質細緻、可見核仁，外圍為中等量灰藍色細胞質並帶少許空泡；形態偏單核球樣，但譜系需靠流式細胞儀確認為混合表型急性白血病。
features: Cluster of intermediate to large blasts with high N:C ratio
Nuclei round to indented/folded, some with cleft or notched contours
Fine, dispersed chromatin with small but discernible nucleoli
Moderate grey-blue to basophilic cytoplasm with scattered fine vacuoles; no Auer rods seen
Occasional smaller cell with more condensed chromatin; background red cells and smudged nuclear material
60147.describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cluster of intermediate to large blasts with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, round to indented and folded nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, and small visible nucleoli. The cytoplasm is moderate in amount, grey-blue to basophilic, and contains scattered fine vacuoles; no Auer rods or distinct granules are identified. Normal maturing hematopoietic elements are not evident in this field. Findings are consistent with acute leukemia with markedly increased blasts; the monocytoid nuclear folding raises myelomonocytic differentiation, and in the setting of immunophenotypic B-lymphoid co-expression and KMT2A rearrangement, the findings support mixed phenotype acute leukemia.

ddx.vs: Morphology overlaps completely, so exclusion relies on flow cytometry showing no B-lineage (CD19 with strong CD79a/CD22/CD10) or T-lineage (cytoplasmic CD3) commitment.
KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL (often CD10-negative) lacks MPO and monocytic markers, whereas MPAL shows a second myeloid/monocytic component.
APL-M3v has bilobed/folded nuclei but typically shows fine granules, strong MPO, CD34/HLA-DR negativity, and PML::RARA.

61619.recognize_zh: 此周邊血液視野只有一顆有核細胞：核呈不規則摺疊或雙葉狀、染色質中度凝集，細胞質布滿細小紫色顆粒，較像未成熟或異常的顆粒球系細胞；本視野看不到典型胚細胞，單張圖無法診斷 CEBPA 突變 AML，需參考病例的血球計數與分子檢測。
features: Single nucleated cell, slightly larger than a mature neutrophil
Irregular, folded to bilobed nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin; nucleoli not evident
Cytoplasm filled with fine purple-lilac granules extending to the cell border
No Auer rods identified; no blasts present in this field
Red cells largely normocytic with occasional fragmented/helmet-shaped forms; platelets not evident
61619.describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single granulated myeloid cell with an irregular, folded to bilobed nucleus, moderately condensed chromatin, and cytoplasm filled with fine purple granules; the cell likely represents an immature or atypical granulocytic element. No blasts or Auer rods are present in this field. The red cells are mostly normocytic, with rare fragmented forms. This single field is non-diagnostic on its own; the diagnosis of AML with mutated CEBPA rests on blast enumeration in blood and marrow and demonstration of an in-frame bZIP CEBPA mutation.

ddx.vs: Basophils have coarse, dark purple-black granules that obscure the nucleus, whereas this cell shows finer lilac granules with a visible folded nucleus.
Monocytic cells have grey-blue cytoplasm with sparse fine granules, vacuoles, and delicate folded chromatin rather than densely granulated cytoplasm.
Reactive immature granulocytes accompany toxic granulation and a normal maturation sequence without circulating blasts, which requires clinical and marrow correlation.
